chunks: From him (Al-Shaykh) he said: Ja'far and Abu Shu'ayb narrated to him from Abu Jamilah from Zayd al-Shahham from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Any man who has sexual intercourse with a slave girl unlawfully (not his own), then buys her and claims her child, he is not inherited from (by that child). For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The child belongs to the bed (of the father), and for the adulterer is the stone (of exclusion).' And the child of the fornicator is not inherited from, except by a man who claims the child of his slave girl."

key_terms.اَلْوَلَدُ لِلْفِرَاشِ: The child belongs to the bed (legitimacy follows the context of union)
key_terms.حَرَاماً: Unlawfully / Not in a formal marriage contract
key_terms.لِلْعَاهِرِ اَلْحَجَرُ: For the fornicator is the stone (exclusion)

ai.seo_question: Does a master inherit from the child of his slave girl if he had unlawful intercourse with her and claims the child?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the asymmetrical inheritance rules for a master who claims paternity of a child born to his slave girl via unlawful intercourse (zina). While the child inherits from the master, the master does not inherit from the child, a ruling derived from the maxim 'the child belongs to the bed' and the exclusion of the fornicator. This specific exception highlights the Shia juristic view that paternity can be established through the master's claim even without a formal marriage contract, provided the mother is his slave.
